ambiguities: The perturbations are arbitrary real labels at internal nodes. No floating-point format, rounding rule, probabilistic model, or realizability condition is specified.
The target proof is excluded from the dossier. The translation describes the supplied proposition and definitions, without auditing its proof.

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This is the sole explicit hypothesis: every internal-node perturbation has absolute value at most the same real u.
dependency_coverage.meaning: For every n ∈ ℕ, t ∈ T_n, e ∈ E(t), and u ∈ ℝ, define B(e,u) recursively by B(leafError,u) = True and B(nodeError(eL,eR,δ),u) = B(eL,u) ∧ (B(eR,u) ∧ |δ| ≤ u).
dependency_coverage.name: Uniform perturbation bound

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The variable errors specifies one real perturbation at each internal node of the given tree.
dependency_coverage.meaning: E(t), for n ∈ ℕ and t ∈ T_n, is an inductive type of decorations of t. Its constructors are leafError ∈ E(leaf) and nodeError(eL,eR,δ) ∈ E(node(l,r)) for eL ∈ E(l), eR ∈ E(r), and δ ∈ ℝ.
dependency_coverage.name: Tree-indexed perturbation decorations

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This is the perturbed evaluation on the left side of the asserted identity.
dependency_coverage.meaning: For n ∈ ℕ, t ∈ T_n, e ∈ E(t), and v : Fin n → ℝ, define R(e,v) recursively. At a leaf, R(leafError,v) = v(0). For l ∈ T_m, r ∈ T_k, and e = nodeError(eL,eR,δ), set R(e,v) = (R(eL,vL) + R(eR,vR))(1+δ), where vL(i)=v(i) for i<m and vR(j)=v(m+j) for j<k.
dependency_coverage.name: Multiplicatively perturbed tree summation

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The right side sums this list with initial ancestor factor 1. Each internal node contributes its exact subtree sum times its own perturbation and all strict-ancestor factors.
dependency_coverage.meaning: For A ∈ ℝ, n ∈ ℕ, t ∈ T_n, e ∈ E(t), and v : Fin n → ℝ, define the real list C(A,e,v). At a leaf it is empty. At e = nodeError(eL,eR,δ), with underlying t = node(l,r), it is (C(A(1+δ),eL,vL) ++ C(A(1+δ),eR,vR)) ++ [(A S(t,v))δ]. Thus entries occur in left-subtree, right-subtree, current-node order.
dependency_coverage.name: Ancestor-weighted error contribution list

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The target ranges over finite ordered full binary summation trees indexed by their number of leaves.
dependency_coverage.meaning: T_n, indexed by n ∈ ℕ, is the inductively generated family with leaf ∈ T_1 and node(l,r) ∈ T_(m+k) for l ∈ T_m and r ∈ T_k. There is no empty-tree constructor.
dependency_coverage.name: Leaf-count-indexed binary trees

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This supplies the exact reference value subtracted from R and the exact subtree sums used in C.
dependency_coverage.meaning: For n ∈ ℕ, t ∈ T_n, and v : Fin n → ℝ, define S(t,v) recursively by S(leaf,v)=v(0) and S(node(l,r),v)=S(l,vL)+S(r,vR). This is the exact real sum of the n leaf entries in their tree order.
dependency_coverage.name: Exact tree summation

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Implements the leaf and node cases in the definition of B without adding a hypothesis.
dependency_coverage.meaning: For any universe level q and family M(n,t,e,u) : Sort q, given n, t ∈ T_n, e ∈ E(t), u ∈ ℝ, a value of M(1,leaf,leafError,a) for every a ∈ ℝ, and a value of M(m+k,node(l,r),nodeError(eL,eR,δ),a) for every m,k,l,r,eL,eR,δ,a of the corresponding types, this dependent case splitter returns M(n,t,e,u). It uses equality transports to align indices and provides no recursive hypotheses.
dependency_coverage.name: Decoration case analysis with a real parameter

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Packages recursive results for B, R, and C; the child results accessed in their definitions are the first components of the respective child packages.
dependency_coverage.meaning: For any family M(n,t,e) : Sort q, define a descendant-result type D_M(e) : Sort(max(1,q)). At leafError it is the singleton type PUnit. At nodeError(eL,eR,δ) it is (M(m,l,eL) × D_M(eL)) × (M(k,r,eR) × D_M(eR)), using universe-polymorphic products.
dependency_coverage.name: Decoration descendant-result packages

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Provides the structural recursive mechanism defining B, R, and C.
dependency_coverage.meaning: For any M(n,t,e) : Sort q, any n,t,e, and a step F which for every n,t,e maps D_M(e) to M(n,t,e), return the recursively constructed value of M(n,t,e). The body takes the first component of the value-and-descendants pair constructed by D020.

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Leaves have no perturbation parameter, are evaluated exactly, satisfy B for every u, and contribute no list entries.

binders: For every natural number n, implicitly quantified.
For every real input vector v : Fin n → ℝ.
For every perturbation decoration errors ∈ E(t), whose type depends on t and n.
Given a proof of B(errors,u), conclude the stated equality. There are no existentially chosen quantities.
conclusions: Equivalently, the signed total evaluation error equals the sum over internal nodes p of S_p δ_p ∏_{a a strict ancestor of p}(1+δ_a), where S_p is the exact sum of the original inputs in p's subtree. The list enumerates nodes in left-right-root postorder, and an empty ancestor product is 1.
The conclusion is an exact real identity. It contains no u, inequality, absolute total-error estimate, or vector norm.
hypotheses: B(errors,u): every internal-node real perturbation δ satisfies |δ| ≤ u.
No explicit assumption requires u ≥ 0 or u < 1.
There are no sign restrictions on v, no balancing or height restrictions on t, and no restrictions on the perturbations beyond B.
There is no floating-point implementation or rounding rule in the proposition; the evaluation is the recursively defined real-arithmetic perturbation model.
mathematical_definitions: T_n denotes LocalDef005 n. Its constructors are leaf ∈ T_1 and node(l,r) ∈ T_(m+k) for l ∈ T_m and r ∈ T_k. These are finite ordered full binary trees with exactly n leaves.
E(t) denotes LocalDef002 t. Its constructors are leafError ∈ E(leaf) and nodeError(eL,eR,δ) ∈ E(node(l,r)), with eL ∈ E(l), eR ∈ E(r), and δ ∈ ℝ.
For v : Fin(m+k) → ℝ, define vL : Fin m → ℝ by vL(i)=v(i), and vR : Fin k → ℝ by vR(j)=v(m+j), using the specified finite-index embeddings.
S denotes LocalDef006: S(leaf,v)=v(0), and S(node(l,r),v)=S(l,vL)+S(r,vR).
B denotes LocalDef001: B(leafError,u)=True, and B(nodeError(eL,eR,δ),u)=B(eL,u) ∧ (B(eR,u) ∧ |δ|≤u). Here |δ|=max(δ,−δ).
C denotes LocalDef004. For every real ancestor factor A, C(A,leafError,v)=[], and C(A,nodeError(eL,eR,δ),v)=(C(A(1+δ),eL,vL) ++ C(A(1+δ),eR,vR)) ++ [(A S(node(l,r),v))δ].
List concatenation preserves order. List sum is the right-associated fold with real addition and terminal zero.
The target uses A=1. Therefore the factor reaching any internal node is the product of 1+δ over its strict ancestors, excluding that node itself.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every finite ordered full binary tree t with n leaves, every assignment v of real inputs to those leaves, every assignment errors of a real perturbation to each internal node, and every real u bounding the absolute value of all those perturbations, evaluate each leaf exactly and each internal node by adding its two recursively evaluated children and multiplying by 1 plus its own perturbation. The resulting value minus the exact sum of the inputs equals the sum of the recursively generated contributions C(1,errors,v): each internal node contributes its exact subtree sum times its own perturbation times the factors 1 plus the perturbations of all its strict ancestors.

vacuity_risks: T_0 is empty because the only base constructor has one leaf and every node adds two positive leaf counts. Thus the universally quantified n=0 case has no tree instances.
If u<0 and the tree has an internal node, B(errors,u) is impossible because |δ|≥0. Such conditional instances are vacuous.
For a single-leaf tree, B is True for every real u, C is empty, and R=S=v(0); the conclusion reduces to 0=0.

The bound hypothesis is algebraically unnecessary for this identity: the recursive formulas give the same decomposition for arbitrary real perturbations. Its presence restricts the formal statement but supplies no quantitative bound in the conclusion.
The proposition is not globally vacuous: every such tree admits the decoration with all perturbations zero, which satisfies B whenever u≥0.
